title: ROME aligned/private rank and payload frontier
hypothesis: A rank-2 shared edit basis plus private residual basis traces a quality/bytes frontier as private edit rank grows; the Mirror split must outperform ordinary joint low-rank edits.

task.keys: one-hot schema-indexed ROME keys, IDs charged

storage: Actual serialized inference .npz bytes, including base layer, all basis matrices, per-edit shared/private codes, key IDs and metadata. Also report edit-state-only serialized bytes.
success_gate: For aligned true-private rank 0 and 2: efficacy nRMSE <=1e-5, locality <=1e-6, complete payload <=70% independent. Mirror-specific success additionally requires a strict frontier gain over ordinary joint low-rank control at matched quality.
failure_gate: No aligned quality/storage point or exact/equal native joint low-rank frontier. Fresh sealed on failure.
boundaries: Private coefficients are supplied by edit request; held-out edits do not train bases
